_readme: Accepted-measurement policies for AnonRouter's OWN confidential gateway (the
first of the two hops this SDK verifies). The second hop, the upstream model
provider's enclave, is pinned separately in measurements.json.
THIS FILE MUST NEVER BE FETCHED FROM THE GATEWAY IT DESCRIBES. A verifier that
downloads its allowlist from the server it is verifying can always be handed an
allowlist naming that server. It ships inside the published packages instead, and
the CI parity gate proves the JS and Python copies never drift.
status=published  a released plane, resolved by verifyGateway() by default.
status=candidate  a reviewed but pre-release plane whose pins are expected to
move. Requires allowCandidate: true, so a default call can
never quietly pass against a plane that is not released.
Every switch in a policy is REQUIRED. A truncated or hand-edited policy fails to
parse rather than silently disabling a check.

policies.notes: AnonRouter confidential data plane on Phala prod5 (Intel TDX, dstack). Reviewed from release manifest anonrouter-tee@731c719, whose deployment reports transport in-tee-tls on a live TDX host. Held at candidate because the plane is pre-release: these pins move on every release, and the residual-work list for the two-plane build is not closed. requireHardwareVerified is true as reviewed, so verification fails closed with reason quote_signature_chain unless you supply your own DCAP chainVerifier; this package deliberately ships none. KNOWN STALE as of 2026-08-29: the live origin was observed serving release anonrouter-tee@xl-7b1b12a, so app_id_pinned, compose_hash_pinned, release_pinned and platform_measurements_pinned all fail against it today. That is the pin doing its job, not a defect. Do NOT refresh these values by copying what the server returned; that is circular. Capture a candidate with scripts/capture-gateway-pins.mjs, then review it against the release manifest for the build you actually intend to trust before promoting it.
